name: East Slope

pitch_detail.notes: Steep climbers' path up Lucky Ridge, then a rope-up glacier traverse across the Borealis Glacier to the Primus-Tricouni saddle.
Talus/scree east slope scramble to the summit.

descent_text: From the summit, downclimb the East Ridge back to Lucky Pass and descend the same eastern-margin line on the Borealis Glacier used on the ascent, staying off the central icefall. There is no established rappel line; parties without a rope can generally walk this off in good conditions, but carry a rope/pickets in case of deteriorating snow bridges.
approach: Start at the Thunder Creek Trailhead at Colonial Creek Campground on SR 20 (turn in just past milepost 130). Follow the Thunder Creek Trail roughly 6-6.7 miles to McAllister Camp, then continue about half a mile and leave the maintained trail, dropping steeply to cross Thunder Creek, to climb the climbers' path up 'Lucky Ridge' to a bivy near the northeast corner of the lake at the toe of the Borealis Glacier (~6,000 ft). Expect about 8 1/4 miles and 4,800 ft of gain from the trailhead to this camp, roughly 9 hours with an overnight pack. Note: the footbridge that once crossed Thunder Creek near McAllister Camp is gone, so the crossing is a log jam or a wade — check current park trail conditions before you go.
overview: The East Slope (East Ridge from Lucky Pass) is Primus Peak's standard, easiest line — Class 2-3 rock and moderate glacier travel above a long backcountry approach up Thunder Creek. It's the most commonly described route on the peak, often combined with neighboring Tricouni Peak (8,102 ft) from the same col.
beta: Little more than a walk once the Lucky Pass col is reached — the difficulty of this route lies almost entirely in the approach (creek crossing, steep brushy ridge gain, and a glacier traverse), not the summit scramble itself. Most parties treat it as a 2-3 day backcountry trip out of Colonial Creek Campground.
gear: Glacier rope (30m+), harness, crevasse-rescue kit, pickets
Approach shoes or light boots for the Class 3 rock finish
